item.title: Ongoing Concern: Litter Bin Still Appears Not to Be Checked at Weekends, 7th August
item.description:
I am writing to raise an ongoing and urgent concern regarding the litter bin located in the alleyway adjacent to 79 King Hall Road, leading towards Clock House Station. The bin is frequently overflowing, resulting in a substantial accumulation of rubbish in the surrounding area. This situation has led to increased vermin activity, including rats and foxes, and poses a clear health and safety risk to both residents and pedestrians. The excessive waste creates unpleasant odours, hygiene concerns, and potential hazards such as slips and trips. Despite previous assurances from Bromley Council that the location would be monitored and serviced over the weekend, the bin remains full and litter continues to accumulate around it. As a result, I do not consider the issue to have been resolved, despite being advised that it had been fixed. It appears that this location may be regularly overlooked during routine waste collection rounds. To help prevent recurring problems and maintain an acceptable standard of cleanliness, I would strongly recommend increasing the collection frequency to at least four times per week. In addition, the bin should be inspected and emptied during weekends (Saturday and/or Sunday) to prevent overflow and ensure the area remains safe and presentable for public use. I respectfully request that this matter be investigated as a priority and that a long-term solution be implemented to ensure the bin is regularly maintained and the surrounding area kept clean. Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving an update on the actions that will be taken to resolve this ongoing issue.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Kings Hall Road, Penge, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
